question: A literary translation service has a first LLM produce a translation, then a second LLM critiques its nuance and idiom accuracy and sends feedback back to the first LLM for revision, repeating across several rounds until the critique passes. Which pattern does this describe?
options: A) Routing, classifying the source text by genre and sending it to a genre-specific translation prompt
B) Parallelization by voting, producing several translations at once and selecting the one preferred by majority vote
C) Evaluator-optimizer, iterating between a generator LLM and a separate evaluator LLM until quality criteria are met
D) Prompt chaining, translating the text once and then passing the result through a formatting-only validation step
correct_answers: C) Evaluator-optimizer, iterating between a generator LLM and a separate evaluator LLM until quality criteria are met
explanations: Incorrect. Routing makes a single upfront classification decision; the scenario describes repeated iterative feedback loops, not a one-time category selection.
Incorrect. Voting produces several independent attempts and picks a winner by majority; the scenario describes iterative refinement of a single translation, not selection among parallel attempts.
Correct. A generator and a distinct evaluator LLM iterating through feedback rounds until a quality bar is met is the defining shape of evaluator-optimizer.
Incorrect. Prompt chaining with a single validation gate does not involve iterative rounds of critique and revision toward a quality target.
